title: Verifier–Agent Co-Design Reduces Verifier-Induced Blocking in Agentic NetOps Planning
abstract: We test whether integrating runtime verifier feedback into an LLM planner (co‑design) reduces verifier‑induced blocking of safe plans relative to a static post‑hoc verifier for synthetic NetOps change tasks. Following a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1), we executed 200 intent→configuration tasks in a deterministic containerized emulator using a hosted gpt-5-mini adapter. Primary analysis used complete paired runs (N=187): guarded planning achieved 187/187 safe completions (1.000) versus 179/187 (0.9572) for baseline; paired absolute difference = 0.04278074866310155, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0078125, paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.016042780748663103, 0.0748663101604278] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Per a reviewer request, we report a preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats incomplete pairs as failures (N=200): contingency counts n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=13 → baseline 179/200 = 0.895, guarded 187/200 = 0.935, paired difference = 0.04, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0078125 (discordant counts unchanged). The bootstrap CI for the sensitivity scenario was not produced by the registered executor and therefore is not reported here. The preregistered secondary non‑inferiority hypothesis on planning latency (H2) is unconfirmed: the registered analysis executor did not produce the paired latency diagnostics required for that test and those diagnostics are absent from the archived analysis outputs. We provide deterministic execution and analysis artifact pointers and discuss validity limits and operational implications.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs and agentic orchestration frameworks are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation and automated change planning. Recent surveys emphasise that operational reliability depends on orchestration, verifier design, and runtime tooling rather than raw model token accuracy [https://openalex.org/W7161354925, https://openalex.org/W7114889968]. A recurring operational tension is the “verifier tax”: aggressive validators reduce unsafe actions but may also block otherwise safe plans unless planners adapt to verifier constraints [https://openalex.org/W7203715746]. We evaluate whether verifier–agent co‑design—making deterministic verifier feedback available at planner runtime and permitting bounded repair—reduces verifier‑induced blocking without materially degrading planning latency. Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment comparing static post‑hoc verification (baseline) to guarded planning with runtime verifier feedback on 200 synthetic tasks; (2) confirmatory evidence that co‑design reduced verifier blocking in this emulated corpus (absolute +0.04278, p=0.0078125); (3) a preregistered sensitivity treatment (incomplete pairs as failures) computed from archived artifacts and disclosure of unexecuted preregistered latency diagnostics.
sections.related_work: Surveys and method reviews document a rapid rise in LLM‑based NetOps/AIOps work and call for workflow‑centred evaluation incorporating verifiers, orchestration, rollback semantics, and trace quality [https://openalex.org/W7161354925, https://openalex.org/W7114889968]. Generate–validate–repair and tool‑augmented agent designs improve grounding but do not eliminate structured‑output failures; runtime monitoring can reduce unsafe actions but creates the verifier‑tax trade‑off we target experimentally [https://openalex.org/W7114889968, https://openalex.org/W7203715746]. Prior work motivates a focused empirical test of verifier–agent co‑design rather than a broad multi‑model leaderboard.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1 before observing outcomes. The confirmatory design is paired: each synthetic task instance (Nplanned=200) was executed twice (baseline: static post‑hoc verifier; guarded: runtime verifier feedback with up to one repair attempt). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar with a paired bootstrap 95% CI (resamples=10000, seed=1729). Generation semantics: preregistered shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation=false). For each task a single initial candidate configuration was generated (shared_initial_generation) and both conditions started from that candidate; guarded planning could then observe deterministic verifier feedback and optionally invoke one repair. Execution contracts, retry/exclusion rules, and deterministic validator semantics are described in the preregistration and followed strictly. Data sources and scoring: deterministic synthetic task generator and containerized emulator images (two topology classes). A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) checked syntax, policy/workflow constraints, and semantic requirements; only runs with validator.final_state.valid==true and all workflow constraints satisfied were scored as safe completions. Analysis executor: confirmatory outputs were produced by registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' (analysis artifacts referenced below). Sensitivity analysis (incomplete pairs as failures): computed deterministically from archived contingency and missingness artifacts (artifact pointers below) without additional model calls. Latency non‑inferiority (H2): required paired per‑episode latency diagnostics; those diagnostics are absent from the registered executor outputs and from the archived analysis artifacts, so H2 remained unconfirmed.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary dataset: planned_episode_count=400 (200 pairs × 2); completed_episode_count=374; failed_episode_count=26; model_calls_used=208; after deterministic exclusions per preregistration the primary confirmatory dataset comprised 187 complete pairs. Primary confirmatory outcome (complete pairs N=187): baseline_success_count=179/187=0.9572192513368984; guarded_success_count=187/187=1.000; paired contingency n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=0; paired absolute difference=0.04278074866310155; exact McNemar two‑sided p=0.0078125; paired bootstrap 95% CI=[0.016042780748663103,0.0748663101604278] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729). Sensitivity analysis (preregistered): treat incomplete pairs (both_missing_pairs=13) as failures in both conditions (N=200). Using archived paired and missingness artifacts this yields n_11=179, n_10=8, n_01=0, n_00=13 → baseline_successes=179/200=0.895, guarded_successes=187/200=0.935, paired difference=0.04. Exact McNemar two‑sided p remains 0.0078125 because discordant counts (n_10=8, n_01=0) are unchanged by adding concordant failures; the registered analysis executor did not produce a bootstrapped CI for the sensitivity scenario and the bootstrap CI therefore is not reported here. Missingness and exclusions: complete_pairs=187, both_missing_pairs=13 (excluded from primary as preregistered). Repair and stage counts: provider audit shows shared_initial_generation=200 and repair=8 (repair invocations align with the 8 discordant guarded‑only successes). Deterministic artifact pointers (files used to compute primary and sensitivity numbers): analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 prefix d6a5b15571c5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 prefix ef339bafcb0e...), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (sha256 prefix f676a25d4003...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha256 prefix 130f65d3f584...), execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 prefix 6a95bf3e300e...), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 prefix 916b386bd80c...). The initial master‑prompt archive required by the track is provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and preregistration manifest sha256 prefix 668ae85f16e6.... Latency diagnostics (H2): the registered executor's outputs and archived analysis artifacts do not contain the per‑episode paired latency diagnostics required to perform the pre‑registered non‑inferiority test (20% margin). Accordingly H2 is reported as unconfirmed rather than supported.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: In this deterministic synthetic/emulated corpus, runtime verifier feedback with bounded repair increased safe end‑to‑end completion probability by ≈4.28 percentage points on the complete‑pair analysis and by 4.0 percentage points under the conservative sensitivity (incomplete pairs=failures). The exact McNemar p (0.0078125) is unchanged by the sensitivity treatment because discordant counts driving McNemar's test are identical. The repair stage count (repair=8) and n_10=8 support the mechanistic interpretation that guarded planning enabled corrective adaptations to an initial shared candidate that baseline post‑hoc verification would have rejected. Threats to validity: internal validity benefits from deterministic pairing, fixed seeds, and preregistered exclusions, but prompt sensitivity and single‑model dependence remain. Construct validity: the deterministic validator approximates operational correctness via DSL and workflow checks but cannot substitute for human operator judgment or multi‑vendor device semantics. External validity: experiments used a single declared adapter (gpt‑5‑mini), a synthetic task generator, and containerized emulators; results do not establish production safety or cross‑model generality. Unexecuted preregistered analyses and artifact gaps: the registered analysis executor did not produce (a) the preregistered sensitivity bootstrap CI for the incomplete‑pair treatment and (b) the paired per‑episode latency diagnostics required to test the latency non‑inferiority hypothesis H2. We computed the sensitivity point estimates and exact McNemar p deterministically from archived contingency and missingness artifacts (paths and sha256 prefixes cited above); bootstrap CI recalculation and the latency non‑inferiority test require executor outputs or re‑execution of the registered analysis contract and therefore remain unexecuted in this report. Operational implications and next steps: co‑design patterns that surface verifier constraints to planners and permit bounded repair reduce verifier‑induced blocking in the constrained setting tested; next steps are systematic multi‑model replications, richer emulators, and human‑in‑the‑loop latency/throughput evaluations to assess production trade‑offs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment comparing static post‑hoc verification and runtime verifier feedback (co‑design) for LLM‑driven NetOps planning in a deterministic emulated corpus. Guarded planning produced a statistically significant increase in safe completion on complete pairs (N=187; absolute +0.04278074866310155; exact McNemar p=0.0078125; paired bootstrap 95% CI reported above). A preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats incomplete pairs as failures (N=200) yields a paired difference of 0.04 and exact McNemar p=0.0078125 (discordant counts unchanged); the sensitivity bootstrap CI was not produced by the registered executor and is not reported. The preregistered latency non‑inferiority hypothesis (H2) is unconfirmed because required paired latency diagnostics are absent from the archived executor outputs; H2 therefore remains inconclusive. Limitations (single model, synthetic/emulated tasks, and unexecuted preregistered diagnostics) bound generalization. We publish deterministic execution and analysis artifacts and artifact pointers so others can reproduce the reported arithmetic and re‑execute registered analysis contracts where desired.

Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis (registered executor), internal peer‑review checks, and manuscript drafting. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure and rehearsal work occurred before the autonomy lock and are explicitly not used as empirical evidence. Preregistration: study preregistered as CNSM2026-AgenticNetOps-GuardedGVR-v1 (preregistration manifest sha256 prefix 668ae85f16e6...). Orchestration and tools permitted: run used hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter, deterministic synthetic intent→configuration task generator, containerized emulator images (two topology classes), deterministic validator 'deterministic_netops_validator_v5', and a preregistered generate–validate–repair policy allowing up to one repair. Model‑call budget and execution: maximum_model_calls set to 400; actual model_calls_used=208; execution followed the frozen retry and exclusion policy; deterministic retry policy allowed up to two infra retries; incomplete pairs were excluded per preregistration for the primary analysis. Artifact pointers for reproducibility and reviewer‑requested sensitivity computation: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256 prefix d6a5b15571c5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256 prefix ef339bafcb0e...), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (sha256 prefix f676a25d4003...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha256 prefix 130f65d3f584...), execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 prefix 6a95bf3e300e...), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 prefix 916b386bd80c...). Post‑lock human editing: no manual human editing, rewriting, or selective improvement of technical content was performed after the autonomy lock; all manuscript text and analyses are derived from archived autonomous‑run artifacts. Deviations and restarts: execution manifest records completed_episode_count=374, failed_episode_count=26; retries and infra failures were handled per the preregistered retry policy and logged. Limitations of autonomy: internet and hosted‑model access were available to the autonomous pipeline as declared; no private proprietary datasets or restricted human adjudications were used.
limitations: Single‑model limitation: experiments used one declared adapter (gpt‑5‑mini); results may not generalize across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.

Synthetic‑emulation scope: tasks derive from a deterministic synthetic intent→configuration generator and containerized emulator topologies; the deterministic validator approximates operational correctness but does not replicate full production rollback, monitoring, or human‑operator decision processes.
External validity: production networks, multi‑vendor device semantics, and human operator procedures are not represented; results do not establish production safety or readiness.

Latency hypothesis unconfirmed: preregistered non‑inferiority H2 on planning latency was not confirmed because the registered analysis executor did not produce required paired latency diagnostics; H2 remains inconclusive.

Sensitivity bootstrap CI absent: the registered executor did not produce a bootstrapped CI for the preregistered incomplete‑pair sensitivity scenario; we report deterministic point estimates and McNemar p computed from archived contingency/missingness artifacts but not the sensitivity bootstrap CI.

Possible residual pretraining exposure: deterministic contamination checks excluded known pre‑lock artifacts but cannot eliminate uncertainty about broader model pretraining exposure to conceptually similar public artifacts.
